sentences.text: Amendment application has been filed today, is taken on record.

2. Heard Mr. P.K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and Mr. Utsav, learned counsel for the informant/complainant.
3.
By means of this application, learned counsel for the applicant has prayed for impleadment of Sections 409 and 201 IPC in the memo of bail application.
4. Amendment is formal in nature, hence, allowed.
5. Let necessary amendment be carried during the course of the day.
Memo of anticipatory bail application 1.
Heard Mr. P.K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and Mr. Utsav, learned counsel for the informant/complainant.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.01 of 2022, under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468 and 471,
409 and 201 IPC, Police Station Bargarh, District Chitrakoot.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case just to harass the applicant in fact no such incident has taken place as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The applicant has never committed any offence as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The applicant was appointed on the post of Secretary and discharged his duty without any complaint and the applicant is going to retire in the month of March, 2026.
The applicant is suffering from several old age ailments.

As per allegation, a complaint was allegedly filed and in pursuance of the same, an enquiry was conducted and in the enquiry it was found that the government record has been exchanged and has been misplaced.

He further submits that the alleged foul play and disappearance of document is being complaint by one Ramashankar @ Ram Shankar in the year 2019 whereas the applicant was transferred from Gram Panchayat Konia on 08.09.2016 and applicant handed over charge to one Ram Kumar, Gram Panchayat Adhikari, who has received the entire record from the applicant putting his signature.
He further submits that the applicant has neither signed the aforesaid document nor he has engineered/manufactured the same.
The applicant has nothing to do with the manufacturing document.
Applicant has been falsely dragged at the behest of his opponent.

He further submitted that placed co-accused, namely, Munni Devi, who was the then Pradhan, has already been granted anticipatory bail by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated Roop Naryan Singh vs State Of U.P.And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141535824/
2 20.09.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.2877 of 2022

The applicant shall have one week thereafter for filing rejoinder affidavit.

5. List this case on 20.12.2023.
6.

4. Thereafter on 12.02.2024, following order was passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court:-
"1. List revised.

2. Heard Sri P. K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Utsav, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri Bare Lal Bind, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.
3.
Learned counsel for the complainant/informant submits that he has filed his vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant/informant in the office on 09.1.2024.
The same is not on record.
Office to trace it out and place it on the record by the next date.
4. Learned counsel for the complainant/informant further prays for 3 weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
Prayer is allowed.
5. The applicant will have 10 days' thereafter to file rejoinder affidavit, if any.

6. Let the matter be listed on 06.03.2024.
7.
The applicant has been granted interim protection vide order dated 28.11.2023 passed by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court which was subsequently extended vide order dated 20.12.2023.

In view of the same, till the next date of listing or till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C., whichever is earlier, in the event of arrest of the applicant Roop Naryan Singh in Case Crime No. 01 of 2022, u/s 420, 466, 467, 468, 471, 409, 201 I.P.C., P.S. Bargarh, District Chitrakoot, he shall be released on interim anticipatory bail, on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.
50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
Roop Naryan Singh vs State Of U.P.And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141535824/

9. The Investigating Officer is directed to conclude the investigation of the present case in accordance with law expeditiously independently without being prejudice by any observation made by this Court while considering the present anticipatory bail application of the applicant.
10. The applicant is are directed to produce a copy of this order before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned within ten days from today, who shall ensure the compliance of present order.

"
5. Thereafter, this Court after getting information from the State that charge sheet has been submitted in the matter and on 02.05.2025, this Court passed the following order:-
"1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 01 of 2022, under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471, 409, 201 IPC, Police Station- Bargarh, District- Chitrakoot.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.

He next submitted that the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 12.02.2024 granted interim anticipatory bail to the applicant till submission of the police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
Applicant has not misused the interim anticipatory bail granted to him and co-operated in the investigation proceedings.
He further submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

4. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and has submitted that Investigating Officer after collecting evidence,
submitted charge-sheet against the applicant, as such, prima facie offence is made Roop Naryan Singh vs State Of U.P.And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141535824/
4 out against the applicant.

entities.text: Roop Naryan Singh vs State Of U.P.And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant may be rejected.

5. Without expressing any opinion on merits of the case and considering the submissions advanced by counsel for the parties, the nature and gravity of the accusation, I find no good ground for anticipatory bail to the applicant in the aforesaid case.
6. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected.

7. However, if the applicant surrenders before the concerned court within one month from today and applies for bail, the bail application of the applicant shall be decided expeditiously by the court concerned, in accordance with law.

8. For the period of one month from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the Court below, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against him."
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant challenged the order dated 02.05.2024 before the Hon'ble Apex Court by filing Criminal Appeal No.3315 of 2024 arising out of S.L.P. No.6940 of 2024.
The Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 09.08.2024 set aside the impugned orders passed by this Court and remand the matter.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant is apprehensive of imminent arrest.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
8.

Learned AGA has filed a counter affidavit dated 11.11.2025 in which paragraph no.8 clearly states that up till now, charge sheet has not been submitted before this Court and the investigation is pending against the applicant.

9. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
10.
